source_user: Choose between tensor and pipeline parallelism for a latency-sensitive multi-GPU service. State the assumptions needed. Scenario variant 170: include an explicit falsifiable hypothesis and a controlled experiment.
source_assistant: Answer should state assumptions, a falsifiable hypothesis, measurements, expected confounders, and rollback criteria. Minimum technical points: compare per-GPU memory, communication topology, layer partitioning, batch and microbatch behavior, synchronization, latency target, and failure/reconfiguration costs.
corrected_answer: Scenario variant 170: do not select tensor parallelism (TP) or pipeline parallelism (PP) from the label alone; make a workload-specific decision. Assume the model graph, precision, GPU count/type, usable HBM in GiB, interconnect topology, software versions, clocks, request-length and arrival distributions, concurrency, batching policy, and SLOs are fixed and recorded; unknown values are estimates, not facts. Enumerate feasible TP degrees and PP layer partitions. Compare TP shard memory and collective bytes/time, topology locality, synchronization and straggler cost with PP stage balance, activation memory/transfers, layer partitioning, microbatch count, pipeline bubbles, queueing, and failure/reconfiguration cost. Pre-register the falsifiable hypothesis that the selected feasible configuration lowers held-out end-to-end p99 by at least M ms or M% at the target load versus the best alternative, while meeting p50/TTFT/TPOT latency, throughput, error-rate, quality, and availability gates; otherwise call the result inconclusive. Run randomized repeated paired trials on equivalent isolated hardware with identical traces, warm-up, seeds, versions, clocks, and load. Tune on one split and evaluate on a disjoint held-out split stratified by prompt/output length and load. Measure p50/p95/p99 in ms, memory in GiB, bandwidth in GB/s, utilization, collective/synchronization time, stage idle/bubble time, queue depth, throughput in requests/s, and recovery time; report sample counts and confidence intervals. Control confounders including thermal throttling, placement, NUMA, kernel/compiler changes, cache state, admission control, batch formation, and correlated failures. Test only authorized, isolated failure injection; record detection, draining, state recovery, degraded-mode behavior, and reconfiguration time. Roll back to the last known-good configuration if SLO, quality, error, memory-headroom, or availability gates fail, or if the effect is not reproducible. Do not claim a universal winner without target-platform evidence.
risks: M, workload trace, target topology, and feasibility gates are unspecified; no generalized performance claim is justified.
TP collectives and PP bubbles/stage balance are implementation-, topology-, and scheduler-dependent.
evidence_required: Target-platform repeated paired benchmark with pre-registered M, disjoint held-out traces, confidence intervals, SLO/quality/reliability results, and authorized recovery test.
